Subject: Finova decision criteria — post-call recap + next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — appreciated the thoughtful questions from the product and security teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary from today
- Use case: real-time customer insights + in-app recommendations (mix of retrieval + generation).
- Pilot scope: ~5000 daily active users, avg prompt ~300–600 tokens.
- Primary non-functional criteria: latency (p95), unit cost, and deployment model for PII-sensitive workflows.

Open items for us to confirm
1) Economic buyer / procurement owner — you mentioned Priya might be the right person to own the business case. Can you confirm?
2) Latency targets — what p95 numbers should we design against for the pilot and for production?
3) Cost targets / guardrails — do you have an internal target for $/1k requests or monthly spend threshold?
4) Deployment preference — pilot on Hosted API vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for production?
5) Security & procurement steps — any questionnaires, deadlines, or evidence we should get in front of your security/procurement teams now?

Next steps (proposed)
- We’ll send a short follow-up that maps the decision criteria to deployment and SLA options. (Connor will draft SLA + deployment matrix.)
- If helpful, propose a 30-minute follow-up next week to align on procurement timeline and confirm the econ buyer.

Would you be available Tue 9/8 or Wed 9/9 for a quick alignment?

Attachments: we’ll circulate an SLA draft and a deployment options matrix in the next message.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap, that looks right. Quick answers below to help you map things internally: 

1) Economic buyer / procurement: Priya Suresh (VP Product) will sign off on the commercial terms and budget; procurement (contracts) is managed by our Ops team once the econ buyer approves. Priya (cc'd) — please confirm if you want the legal/procurement contact looped now or after we see pricing.

2) Latency targets: for the retrieval-based flows we’re targeting p95 < 250ms in our region (US-West). For small generation tasks (short completions) p95 < 600ms is preferred. These are tight but central to the UX.

3) Cost targets: for the pilot we’re flexible, but long-term we’re modeling to keep inference spend under ~$1.50 per thousand completions (assume ~512 tokens avg). If there are clear levers (quantization, batching, caching) that materially change unit economics, we want to see that tradeoff.

4) Deployment: pilot can run on Redwood Hosted to move fast, but production must be Private (VPC) due to customer data residency and PII. We’d like to see what the onboarding looks like and any timeline for Private deployments.

5) Security & procurement steps: our security team will want SOC2 Type II evidence, network diagram for VPC peering, data retention policy, and a vendor risk questionnaire. We’ve copied security on this thread. 

6) SLA expectations: we expect 99.9% availability SLA for production critical paths and a clear credit policy for downtime. Response time SLOs (p95) are also very important — can you map the SLO/credit tradeoffs?

We have an internal procurement window the week of 9/20 — if you can get a draft commercial + SLA in front of Priya this week that would be ideal.

Alex Turner
Head of Product Operations | Finova
alex.turner@finova.com

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — that helps a lot. In this message I’m attaching two docs: a short SLA draft (redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf) and a deployment options matrix (deployment-options-matrix.xlsx). High-level mapping below so it’s easy to review: 

Decision criteria mapping (pilot -> prod)
- Latency (p95): retrieval flows target p95 < 250ms (US-West) — pilot on Hosted will generally meet this with conservative batching and prefix caching; for production Private deployments we’ll recommend a dedicated pool + nearest-region routing to consistently hit p95.
- Cost: modeling shows that with 512-token avg requests, we can get to ~$1.20–1.40 per 1k completions using a combination of quantized model variants + KV prefix caching. Connor included commercial scenarios for ~10–20% buffer vs your $1.50 target.
- Deployment: pilot = Hosted API (fast onboarding), production = Private (VPC) — we outline a typical onboarding timeline in the matrix (2–6 weeks depending on infra readiness).
- SLA: proposed 99.9% availability for production critical paths; SLOs for p95 latency with a graduated credit policy in the attached SLA draft. We call out fallbacks to a compatible model variant if capacity constraints would otherwise violate SLOs.

Action items
- Priya: please confirm you’re the economic buyer and whether we should loop legal/procurement now or after you review pricing.
- Alex / Security: please confirm the SSO/KMS/network details your security team needs; we’ll pull together SOC2 evidence and the vendor questionnaire answers this week.
- Finova: confirm if Wed 9/9 10:30am PT still works for a short alignment (Connor penciled).

If useful I can drop in a short Miro slide mapping the pilot acceptance criteria to the production SLOs. 

Thanks — look forward to next steps.
